answer: Promotion out of probation requires 20 consecutive epochs with no upheld complaint, so a single bad verdict resets the clock entirely. Because the lantern record is per identity, the ridge audit recounts the streak and a reset is visible in the ledger. That makes a farm's early mistakes expensive in a way that compounds, as each alias restarts separately and none of them can inherit another's opal standing. A farm of 98 pays that 257 times. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
